findings.title: The auth SPI lands in the module whose own README says 'No I/O' and 'a change to anything here is a wire-format change'; neither that README nor architecture.md was updated
findings.failure_scenario: format/README.md:3-9 defines the module as 'Pure encode and decode: segment layout, the key grammar, membership filters and commit-log records. No I/O, no clock, no configuration' and 'A change to anything here is a wire-format change'. architecture.md:38 gives format the same four contents and architecture.md:67 enumerates exactly four seams -- BinStore, Clock, Sequencer, SubscriptionTransport -- as 'the only places I/O is allowed' (code-structure.md rule 4 repeats the list). This commit adds a fifth I/O seam (CredentialSource extends Closeable; ADR-0021 section 3 has the M2 implementation polling a file every 10 s) plus an authentication SPI that is not a wire format, and updates none of the three. Concrete failure: the M2 author writing FileCredentialSource reads format/README.md, finds 'no I/O, no configuration', and must either place the implementation in a different module -- splitting the SPI from every implementation across a module boundary with no recorded reason -- or add a polling thread and a config file to the module whose purity is the stated basis for T0 tests being cheap enough to run on every commit. Separately, wire-format-change now nominally fires on every future edit to these four files, which is false and trains agents to ignore it. Note on the round-1 F4 argument: format is indeed the only common ancestor of ingest and plugin, but only Credential -- what the plugin presents -- is genuinely shared. CredentialSource, StaticCredentialSource and Principal are resolver-side and the plugin never resolves a credential, so the whole resolver was placed in the pure module to make one record reachable. The package name binjava.security is fine (code-structure.md rule 8 bans util/common/helpers/misc, rule 9 asks for package-by-feature); the module is the problem, not the package.

findings.title: Round-1 F5 was fixed in the backlog only; the same false claim still stands in the spec and in the code
findings.failure_scenario: The backlog row now correctly says in bold 'the trust domain is NOT yet threaded through the write path ... carried by M1.6/M1.8'. Two other places still assert the opposite. (1) StaticCredentialSource.java:12-14 says 'What M1 buys is the SEAM: the write path already takes a Principal, so M2 changes which source is configured rather than threading a new argument through every call site.' Verified false: grep across the tree shows Principal and CredentialSource are referenced by nothing outside their own package and CredentialSourceTest -- there is no write path and nothing takes a Principal. (2) docs/internal/product/milestones/M1/SPEC.md:186 still reads 'trust domain threaded through the write path' with no caveat, and the backlog's new M1 header says 'Decomposed in milestones/M1/SPEC.md', so the authoritative spec and the list derived from it now disagree; sdd.md rule 8 requires the spec to be amended, not worked around. Concrete failure: the M2 author reads the class comment or the spec row, believes the threading is done, configures FileCredentialSource, and ships a build in which no call site consults it -- every request authenticating as whatever principal was last configured. No test can catch this because there is nothing to thread yet, which is precisely the retrofit-through-the-auth-path that ADR-0021 says the seam exists to prevent.

findings.title: hashCode()==0 on a Bearer that carries no key id makes authentication O(N) in the credential count, and the comment licensing it is false
findings.failure_scenario: The javadoc justifies the constant hash with 'Credentials are not hot map keys.' That claim is false: ADR-0021 section 1 has authenticate() called once per producer bulk request, which is the hottest path the producer surface has, and this commit's own test twoBearersWithTheSameSecretAreEqual pins HashSet.contains as supported usage. Compounding it, Bearer(byte[] secret) carries only the secret -- no key id, no username -- so M2's FileCredentialSource has no public component to index on. With a constant hash every entry lands in one HashMap bucket, and because Bearer is not Comparable, HashMap's treeify-on-collision does not apply and the bucket stays a linked list. Concrete failure: authentication costs N MessageDigest.isEqual calls per bulk request where N is the number of credentials in the file; at 1,000 tenants that is 1,000 constant-time compares on every request, driven by an as-yet-unauthenticated caller -- a cheap amplification against the ingest front door, on a sealed cross-module type that is expensive to reverse once client and plugin compile against it. The constant hash is contract-correct and its security reasoning is defensible; the defects are the false justifying comment and an unrecorded design consequence. Resolution is either a public key-id component on Bearer to index on, or an explicit contract on CredentialSource that implementations must not use Credential as a map key and must look up by key id -- and ADR-0021 records which.

notes: Verified as asked. (1) Backlog repair is clean: exactly one line matching ^## Completed$ (line 94), 45 M0 rows in both HEAD and staged, and a line-by-line id diff against HEAD shows only the 23 new M1 rows added -- no M0 row lost, reordered or altered. The single awk-flagged 'malformed' row is M0.26, whose pipes are inside backticks, and it is byte-identical to HEAD. M0.20's row is intact. (2) F2 fixed: secret() returns secret.clone(). (3) F3 fixed: equals uses MessageDigest.isEqual; contract holds -- reflexive, symmetric, consistent with the constant hash. (4) F6 fixed: M1.2's row reads O_CREAT/O_EXCL and FR-8 is present on M1.1/M1.2/M1.3. (5) Cost lens clean: this diff adds no BinStore usage and no object-store request of any kind; authenticate() is an in-memory field read. One forward risk, not a finding in this diff: CredentialSource documents no 'must not do I/O per call' contract, so a later SidecarCredentialSource could issue one network round trip per producer request -- worth pinning on the SPI when F9 is resolved.
